payload.summary: Two sessions closing the same ledger row is a race the loser cannot lose gracefully: it hard-fails the planner, its outcome text is discarded, and the archived row cannot then be corrected
payload.detail: Hit and worked through on PR #2521, 2026-09-02, and recorded because the cost fell entirely on the session that did the larger piece of work. THE RACE: two sessions independently queued done requests for #0HYHTH (mine 2a381215, the other 59f035ef) and update-then-done for #AGRAKQ. The reconciliation on main (#2542) applied the other session's requests first. THREE CONSEQUENCES, in increasing order of how badly they behave. (1) The loser does not merely lose. My done for #0HYHTH threw '#0HYHTH is no longer open' and my done for #AGRAKQ threw 'is stale: the ledger row changed after this request was queued', and because docs:check-links runs the planner, BOTH hard-failed an unrelated CI check on a PR whose diff had nothing to do with either row. The branch was blocked until each was cancelled or reissued by hand. (2) A cancel queued against a request that has already been applied silently becomes a no-op: both fd9de7fe and 1e305210 now report 'did not take effect -- the cancellation is recorded but changed nothing; correct the affected row with a new update request'. So an attempt to supersede another session's close leaves a record that reads as an action but is not one. (3) That suggested remedy does not exist for a closed row. issues:update rejects with '#0HYHTH is not in Open items' (scripts/ledger-inbox.mjs, the fingerprint branch requires the row be in Open items), so once the race is lost the winning outcome text is final and the archive cannot be corrected through the tooling at all. CONCRETE DAMAGE, which is also the correction this row exists to carry: #0HYHTH is archived with an outcome describing the interface vocabulary scan as it stood at B3 -- two roots, src/components/caring-contacts/workspace and src/app/caring-contacts -- and naming the sealed domain as outstanding residue. PR #2521 took that scan to FIVE roots, adding src/lib/caring-contacts/**, src/lib/caring-contacts-server/** and src/app/api/caring-contacts/**, which closes the residue the archived text still describes as open. A reader of the archive today would conclude the sealed domain is unwatched. It is not. Treat this row as the correction to that archived outcome, since the archived row itself cannot be amended. CANDIDATE FIXES: make a done request against an already-closed row a warning that no-ops, like the cancel case, rather than a throw, so one session's race loss cannot red an unrelated PR's CI; allow update on an archived row, or provide an explicit amend-outcome action, so a superseded outcome can be corrected rather than being final by accident; and consider having reconcile prefer the LATER of two competing closes for the same row, or at least surface both outcomes, since the second is usually the better-informed one. Related but distinct from #Y090R5, which covers the generated snapshot file conflicting between concurrent inbox PRs.
